plan.title: Heart tissue treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 heart tissue samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples after excluding the metadata self-column) from rRNA-depleted total RNA libraries without UMIs. Two QC flags matter directly: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, and most libraries show duplication >60%. Per grounded RNA-seq guidance, neither is grounds for silent removal or de-duplication without UMIs — both must be surfaced quantitatively in a sample-structure QC step (library size, detected genes, duplication rate side by side, PCA/vst, sample-distance heatmap) before any modeling decision, and the DESeq2 negative-binomial model handles depth differences through size factors rather than by discarding the sample. Strandedness is unknown, which the grounded procedure requires be treated as an open question for the report given no BAM/RSeQC input is available here (counts only) - flagged as a caveat rather than a re-derivable step since only a count matrix, not aligned reads, is provided. The core comparison is treated vs control on filtered, size-factor-normalized counts with a DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05, with edgeR quasi-likelihood run in parallel as the robustness cross-check the procedure recommends for 6-per-group designs. Differentially expressed genes feed a preranked fgsea analysis (ranked on the Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome/WikiPathways/GO-BP (secondary), all confirmed present in the reference store for human. A final report step consolidates DE tables, fit diagnostics, enrichment results with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record.

integrated DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
